# ART MCP server

Lets an LLM (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, any MCP client) edit photos in a
**running** ART instance, through the `ART --cmd ...` remote-command mode (or, without a GUI, through
`ART-cli --server`, see below).

* `art_mcp_server.py` – the server (Python 3, standard library only; MCP over stdio)
* `reference/` – the tool/parameter documentation the LLM reads through the
  `art_reference` tool (and as `art://reference/*` resources). Generated from
  `src/engine/procparams.cc`, the GUI sources and the docs site.
* `known_keys.json` – groups/keys accepted in edits, generated by `gen_keys.py`
  from `procparams.cc` (re-run it when the profile format changes)

> **Opt-in only.** This server is not part of the ART application or its
> installers, ART never starts it and nothing enables it by default: it runs
> only if you add it to an MCP client's configuration, and stops when you
> remove it.
>
> **Privacy.** The server runs locally and contacts nothing, but the MCP client
> sends everything the tools return to the language model's provider: previews
> of your images (also full-resolution crops), file names and paths, the open
> folder, camera/lens/exposure metadata, and your edits. Do not use it on images
> you must not share with that provider. See the "Privacy" section of the user
> documentation (MCP.md on the docs site) for what is sent and how to reduce it.

## Use

ART must be running; the remote commands fail with "no running instance"
otherwise. They use ART's D-Bus session bus (the GApplication single-instance
mechanism), which each platform provides differently:

| platform | bus | what the server does |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | the app launcher (`ART.app/Contents/MacOS/ART`) starts a private bus; its socket is `$TMPDIR/ART-$USER/dbus.sock` | run ART_BIN through the launcher; supply `TMPDIR` when the client has none (Claude Desktop does not) |
| Linux | the desktop session's bus (`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, normally `/run/user/UID/bus`); the bundle ships no daemon | inherit the environment; fall back to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus` |
| Windows | GLib autolaunches a per-install bus through the bundled `gdbus.exe` | nothing; ART_BIN **must be the same installation** as the running ART (detected automatically) |

Register the server, e.g. for Claude Code:

    claude mcp add art -- python3 /path/to/ART/tools/mcp/art_mcp_server.py

or in a client's JSON config (on Windows use `python` or `py` as the command
if `python3` does not exist):

    {"mcpServers": {"art": {"command": "python3",
        "args": ["/path/to/ART/tools/mcp/art_mcp_server.py"],
        "env": {"ART_BIN": "/path/to/ART"}}}}

`ART_BIN` is the ART executable or launcher (`ART.app/Contents/MacOS/ART`, the
bundle's `ART` script or AppImage `AppRun`-launched binary, `ART.exe`). When
unset it is auto-detected: the running instance first, then common install
locations (`~/Applications`, `/Applications`, `/opt/ART`, `%ProgramFiles%\ART`,
...), the build tree and `PATH`. The remote commands run in the GUI process, so
the GUI executable (not `ART-cli`) is what is needed.

## Headless backend (no GUI)

The same tools can drive a headless `ART-cli --server` instead of the GUI: no
desktop session, no D-Bus. Start the server (see `doc/server_mode.md`) and set
`ART_MCP_BACKEND=server` in the MCP server's environment:

    ART-cli --server &
    claude mcp add art -e ART_MCP_BACKEND=server -e ART_CLI_BIN=/path/to/ART-cli \
        -- python3 /path/to/ART/tools/mcp/art_mcp_server.py

The server talks to `ART-cli --cmd` through a Unix socket (`ART_SERVER_SOCKET`
or the default one; both processes must use the same). `ART_CLI_BIN` is found
like `ART_BIN` (next to it, the install locations, the build tree, `PATH`).
With this backend:

* the file browser, rating, colour label and session tools are not offered
  (the server has no file browser); `art_open_image` opens the active image;
* `art_save` is offered: nothing is written to the `.arp` sidecar until it is
  called (the GUI saves when an image is closed);
* `art_get_spot_wb` (both backends) measures the white balance of a rectangle.

`art_status` shows which backend is in use and whether it is reachable.

## Troubleshooting

`art_status` prints the executable and bus it used and, when ART cannot be
reached, the reason. "no running instance" means the client and the GUI do not
share a session bus (or the GUI is not running).

**macOS, Claude Desktop (or any GUI client).** Such clients start the server
with a minimal environment: no `TMPDIR`, no `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`. The
server compensates (it supplies `TMPDIR` and runs ART through the app launcher,
which sets the bus). Set `ART_BIN` to `.../ART.app/Contents/MacOS/ART` of the
copy that is running; a bare build-tree binary has no launcher and no bus.

**Linux without the session bus variable.** If the MCP client does not pass
`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` on (clients started from a launcher, a systemd user
service, `sudo`, a container/flatpak/snap sandbox, or over ssh), the server
falls back to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`, or `/run/user/<uid>/bus`. That works with
systemd-style sessions. It does *not* cover a bus at another path (e.g. started
by `dbus-launch`, or a session using the `dbus-broker` abstract address) or a
sandbox that hides `/run/user/<uid>`. Then set the variable in the server's
`env` to the value ART itself sees (`echo $DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` in a
terminal of the same session, or `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -f .ART.bin)/environ
| grep DBUS`). The server and the GUI must also run as the same user. A GUI
started with `-N`, `-s` or `-gimp` does not use the bus and cannot be driven.
If ART runs inside a sandbox (AppImage is fine; flatpak/snap are not covered),
the server cannot see its bus unless the sandbox exposes it.

**Windows.** (Untested; based on the build files.) The bus is started on demand
by the `gdbus.exe` shipped in the ART install directory, and GLib scopes it to
that install path, so `ART_BIN` must be the very `ART.exe` of the running
instance (auto-detection uses `Get-Process`; if PowerShell is unavailable or
several copies run, set `ART_BIN`). Known risks:
* `ART.exe` is a GUI-subsystem program (`-mwindows`): its command output reaches
  the server only through redirected standard handles. If every command fails
  with an empty or "cannot run" error, run `ART.exe --cmd get-dir` from a
  terminal to see whether any output appears, and report it.
* if the first `ART --cmd` call happens while no ART is running, GLib may start
  an empty bus and the call fails; start ART first.
* use `python` or `py -3` as the client's `command` when `python3` does not exist.
* paths in tool arguments may use either `\` or `/`.

**All platforms.** The remote commands act on the *visible* editor tab; they
wait up to 60 s for the editor to finish loading (error: "timeout waiting for
the editor"), and `ART_MCP_TIMEOUT` (seconds, default 120) bounds each call.
Run `python3 art_mcp_server.py --check` to verify the install without ART.

`python3 art_mcp_server.py --check` prints the tool list and how much
reference material was found.

## Tools

`art_status`, `art_reference`, `art_open_directory`, `art_get_directory`,
`art_open_image`, `art_list_open_images`, `art_get_info`, `art_get_edit`,
`art_apply_edit`, `art_apply_profile_file`, `art_preview`, `art_get_spot_wb`,
`art_get_history`,
`art_undo`, `art_redo`, `art_history_goto`, `art_get_snapshots`, `art_snapshot`,
`art_set_rating`,
`art_set_color_label`, `art_session`; and `art_save` with the headless backend.

Edits (`art_apply_edit`) are written as a partial `.arp` file and applied with
`ART --cmd apply`; names are validated against `known_keys.json` first, so a
typo gives "did you mean ..." instead of being silently ignored.
